question: A 7-year-old boy from a rural area presents with sudden haematemesis and massive splenomegaly. His liver function tests are entirely normal. Abdominal ultrasound shows multiple collateral vessels at the porta hepatis instead of a single portal vein trunk. Which ONE diagnosis BEST explains this picture?

answers.text: Cirrhosis of the liver with intrahepatic portal hypertension and oesophageal varices.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Cirrhosis causes intrahepatic portal hypertension with ABNORMAL liver function tests (elevated bilirubin, low albumin, elevated INR). This child has NORMAL liver function tests, pointing strongly to an extrahepatic cause.

answers.text: Extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO) with cavernous transformation of the portal vein.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. EHPVO is the MOST COMMON cause of portal hypertension in Indian children. It occurs due to portal vein thrombosis (commonly following neonatal umbilical vein catheterisation, sepsis, or dehydration), which organises into a sponge-like network of collaterals at the porta hepatis = 'cavernous transformation'. Key features: normal liver function (no hepatocellular disease), massive splenomegaly, variceal bleeding, hypersplenism (cytopenias). The pathognomonic ultrasound finding = cavernous transformation replacing the portal vein.

answers.text: Hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome) causing post-hepatic portal hypertension.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Budd-Chiari syndrome (hepatic vein occlusion) causes post-sinusoidal portal hypertension with tender hepatomegaly, ascites, and ABNORMAL liver function. The ultrasound in Budd-Chiari shows absent hepatic vein flow and caudate lobe hypertrophy — not cavernous transformation of the portal vein.

answers.text: Congenital hepatic fibrosis causing peri-portal fibrosis and sinusoidal obstruction.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Congenital hepatic fibrosis causes intrahepatic pre-sinusoidal portal hypertension with portal tracts expanded by fibrous tissue. While LFTs can be relatively normal, the ultrasound shows peri-portal fibrosis and hepatomegaly — not cavernous transformation of the main portal vein trunk.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key classification: pre-hepatic (EHPVO — normal LFTs, cavernous transformation), intrahepatic (cirrhosis — abnormal LFTs, shrunken liver), post-hepatic (Budd-Chiari — absent hepatic vein, ascites). In India, EHPVO is the most common cause in children; cirrhosis is more common in adults.

Correct. EHPVO is the commonest cause of paediatric portal hypertension in India. Normal liver function + massive splenomegaly + variceal bleeding + cavernous transformation on USG = EHPVO until proven otherwise. Treatment of acute bleed: resuscitation + IV terlipressin/octreotide + urgent endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) or sclerotherapy.
